findings.title: Other bun:bundle import forms leave unbound identifiers that throw at runtime
findings.body:
The whole import statement is replaced with `S.Empty`, and only the `feature` item gets a declared symbol.

- For any other named specifier, the local binding is never declared. Its references become unbound globals and throw `ReferenceError`, even though the warning says the value "will be undefined".
- `import * as b from "bun:bundle"` and `import d from "bun:bundle"` are dropped silently, with no diagnostic. A later `b.feature("X")` then fails at runtime.

Fix: report namespace, default and unknown specifiers as errors, or declare them so they really evaluate to `undefined`.

findings.title: BundleOptions ends up pointing at a set it does not own, which deinit then frees
findings.body:
`transpiler.options.bundler_feature_flags = &config.features` stores a pointer to a field inside the JS build config. The new `BundleOptions.deinit` frees any pointer that is not the static empty set: it calls `deinit()` and then `allocator.destroy()`.

If this transpiler is ever deinitialised, that pointer was never allocated with `allocator.create`, so `destroy` is an invalid free. `config.deinit()` also frees `self.features`, which makes it a double free. The pointer also becomes dangling if the config is torn down before the transpiler. I could not see whether this transpiler's `deinit` runs on the Bun.build path.

Fix: track ownership explicitly, for example with an `owns_bundler_feature_flags` bool, or clone the set into transpiler-owned memory.

findings.title: Feature flags are not part of the runtime transpiler cache key
findings.body:
`bundler_feature_flags` changes the transpiled output: `feature("X")` becomes `true` or `false`. It is not added to `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler` and is not mixed into the cache hash in any other visible way.

With the runtime transpiler cache on, a file transpiled by `bun run index.ts` is stored with `false` baked in. A later `bun run --feature=X index.ts` (or `bun test --feature=X`) can load that cached output and still see `false`, and the reverse also happens. This only affects files large enough to be cached, so the result depends on file size.

Fix: fold the sorted flag set into the cache hash, or skip the cache when any flag is set or the file imports `bun:bundle`.

held.title: Feature-flag set is allocated twice; the first copy leaks
held.body: `BundleOptions.fromApi` already builds `bundler_feature_flags` from `ctx.args.feature_flags`, assuming the transpiler is initialised from `ctx.args`. This line then builds a second set and overwrites the pointer, so the first allocation is never freed. Drop the reassignment here, or only assign when the field is still the empty set.
